jobs.description:
Company Description

Alfa-Leasing has been partnering with entrepreneurs for over 26 years, creating leasing solutions that support businesses of all sizes across Russia. The company provides passenger and commercial vehicles, trucks, special equipment, trailers, semi-trailers, and a wide range of equipment on flexible terms, including options with a 0% advance payment. Alfa-Leasing focuses on helping clients start generating income from the first day of the lease by offering fast, convenient service tailored to business needs. The company values strong client relationships, collaborative teamwork, accountability for results, and an entrepreneurial mindset that seeks flexible, proactive solutions. These principles drive continuous improvement of products and services for clients in diverse industries.

Role Description

The Vice President Information Technology role is a full-time, remote leadership position responsible for overseeing Alfa-Leasing’s technology strategy and operations. This role leads the IT organization, aligning systems, infrastructure, and applications with business goals and regulatory requirements. Daily responsibilities include defining and executing IT strategy, prioritizing and managing technology projects, and driving digital transformation initiatives that enhance efficiency, security, and client experience. The Vice President Information Technology collaborates with senior leadership and cross-functional teams to plan technology investments, manage budgets, and ensure reliable IT services. The role also guides IT governance, risk management, and vendor relationships, while building and mentoring a high-performing IT team.

Strong foundation in Information Technology with experience overseeing enterprise systems, infrastructure, and applications.
Proven IT Management skills, including team leadership, budgeting, vendor management, and operational oversight.
Demonstrated ability to develop and execute IT Strategy aligned with business objectives and regulatory requirements.
Solid Project Management capabilities for planning, implementing, and monitoring complex technology initiatives.
Expertise in Strategic Planning, including long-term technology roadmapping and prioritization of investments.
Experience in financial services, leasing, or related industries is beneficial.
Knowledge of information security, data privacy, and IT risk management best practices.
Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and decision-making skills.
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related field.
Fluency in Russian and proficiency in English are advantageous for collaboration and documentation.

jobs.title: Internal Audit Executive Director – Global Audit Lead, Cybersecurity, Information Security & Cyber Resilience
jobs.description:
The cyber risk landscape is changing rapidly, and the Firm requires audit leadership equipped to meet the moment. We are seeking an Executive Director to lead internal audit technology coverage across the global Firm and its banking entities, including Morgan Stanley Bank, N.A. (MSBNA) and Morgan Stanley Private Bank, N.A. (MSPBNA). This role demands a forward-looking leader who can address both today's threats and the emerging risks now reshaping cybersecurity, information security, and cyber resilience — with deep cyber risk expertise and a strong understanding of how artificial intelligence, agentic and frontier AI models, cloud transformation, and digital assets are actively changing the risk landscape and regulatory expectations. The successful candidate will translate these developments into practical, risk-based audit strategies, deliver insightful challenge to management, and evolve the Firm's assurance approach to address current and emerging threats.

The Internal Audit Division (IAD) drives attention and resources to vulnerabilities by providing an independent and well-informed view and impactful messages about the most important risks facing our Firm. This is accomplished by performing a range of assurance activities to independently assess the quality and effectiveness of Morgan Stanley’s system of internal control, including risk management and governance systems and processes. IAD serves as an objective and independent function within the Firm’s risk management framework to foster continual improvement of risk management processes. This is an Executive Director (P6) level position within the Technical Specialist function, which is responsible for providing extensive subject matter expertise and reinforcing the ability of business and technology audit teams to appropriately assess risk and determine and execute coverage.

Since 1935, Morgan Stanley is known as a global leader in financial services, always evolving and innovating to better serve our clients and our communities in more than 40 countries around the world.

What You’ll Do In The Role

Prioritize and lead coverage of emerging risks related to artificial intelligence and frontier models — including generative and agentic AI — assessing build time, run time, and life cycle controls, data protection, identity and entitlements for autonomous agents, and the expanded attack surface these capabilities create, as well as adversaries’ growing use of AI to accelerate and scale attacks.
Provide coverage of the idiosyncratic risks arising from cryptocurrency and digital assets, including digital asset custody, private key generation and lifecycle management, and the security of both online (network-connected) and offline (air-gapped) custody infrastructure — highlighting the associated cyber threats such as private key compromise, transaction and address manipulation, smart contract exploitation, and the irreversible loss of assets.
Assess quantum computing and post-quantum cryptography readiness, and other frontier technology risks, ensuring these are reflected in the audit plan and in the Firm’s forward-looking resilience posture.
Monitor the intensifying threat landscape — including advanced attack techniques and regulatory change — and continuously factor emerging threats into audit scoping and assurance coverage.
Provide independent assurance over the design and operating effectiveness of the controls that protect the Firm’s and Banks’ technology environment, customer data, and critical business services
Set and lead the multi-year, risk-based audit strategy for cybersecurity, information security, and cyber resilience across the Firm and its Banks, spanning the full technology stack (infrastructure, network, platform, application, and data layers) and each business unit to form an integrated, Firm-wide view of control effectiveness, and how cyber threats, information loss, and a cyber attach could affect business lines, critical services, and legal entities across the Firm.
Direct execution of the audit plan across the core cyber and information security domains — identity and access management, endpoint security, network security, data protection, threat detection and response, and vulnerability management.
Lead assurance activities assessing cyber resilience capabilities, including incident response, disaster recovery, business continuity, and third-party/vendor security.
Evaluate compliance with regulatory expectations (e.g., FFIEC, OCC, FDIC, NYDFS, GLBA, RGF, DORA) and industry frameworks (CRI Profile, NIST CSF, ISO 27001).
Oversee root cause analysis on control failures and audit findings, and track remediation to closure.
Comprehensively articulate actionable insights regarding the criticality and impact of cyber risk, and how well it is managed, to senior management and regulators. Prepare materials for the Chief Audit Executive’s updates to the Audit Committee and the Board,
Coordinate with second-line risk and compliance functions and with external auditors and regulators, and collaborate with global peers to identify risk themes and implications across business segments and legal entities.
Mentor and develop audit staff and manage a global team; help inform and address talent needs and identify stretch and development opportunities for team members.

What You’ll Bring To The Role

Advanced understanding of cybersecurity, information security, and cyber resilience risks and the relevant regulations, including banking regulatory requirements.
Experience assessing emerging technology risks and their control implications — including AI and agentic AI, frontier models, cryptocurrency and digital asset custody, and quantum/post-quantum cryptography — and the ability to translate a rapidly changing threat landscape into practical audit coverage.
Strong knowledge of cybersecurity frameworks (NIST CSF, ISO 27001, CRI Profile) and experience auditing identity and access management, cloud security, and network architecture.
Expertise in audit principles, methodology, tools, and processes (e.g., risk assessments, planning, testing, reporting, and continuous monitoring).
Ability to analyze data and prioritize coverage and assurance activities based on the criticality of risk.
Ability to articulate risk and impact clearly and succinctly to different audiences, including senior stakeholders, the Board, and regulators.
Ability to inspire and support others to do their best work through active coaching, feedback, and development opportunities, and by ensuring trust and inclusion among team members.
Experience in overseeing resource utilization and monitoring progress against deliverables.
A bachelor’s degree in Information Security, Computer Science, or a related field.
At least 12-15 years’ relevant experience in IT/cyber audit, information security, or risk management — ideally in banking or financial services — would generally be expected to fulfill the skills required for this role.
Relevant certifications (e.g., CISA, CISSP, CISM, or equivalent) preferred.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with incident response or red team/penetration testing programs.
Familiarity with the MITRE ATT&CK framework.
Prior experience at a large financial institution or a Big 4 consulting firm.

WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT FROM MORGAN STANLEY

Our values — putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back — aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what’s best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. Hundreds of microservices, primarily Java, running in the cloud.

Drive scalability, resilience, disaster recovery, and cloud cost efficiency.

High 5 Games is hiring a Director of Technology who is first and foremost a hands-on chief architect. You will shape the technical vision and grow into owning the architecture of a cloud platform built on hundreds of Java microservices that process millions of real-time transactions every day.

You will join a mature, high-volume platform that is already running in production. You'll spend your first 90 days learning it deeply, embedded with the teams that built it, and take ownership of its architecture domain by domain: starting with the data and transaction layer, then service architecture and the cloud platform. By the end of your first year, you'll own the platform's architecture end to end and set its direction for the years ahead.

This is not a slide-deck architect role. You will design systems, review code and schemas, set engineering standards, and lead the engineering and technology teams that build and run the platform. You must be comfortable explaining technology strategy and trade-offs to executives, business partners, and regulators.

The platform you will own

Hundreds of microservices, primarily Java, running in the cloud.
Millions of real-time transactions per day, where latency, consistency, and auditability matter on every one.
Regulated, money-adjacent workloads for social and sweepstakes casino gaming: wallets, purchases, game outcomes, and promotions.
24x7 availability for players across web and mobile.

Responsibilities

Architecture and system design

Take ownership of the microservices platform's architecture, domain by domain, through the first year, and then own it end to end: service boundaries, APIs, data ownership, and inter-service communication.
Design for high-volume, low-latency, real-time transaction processing with strong consistency and idempotency guarantees.
Define patterns for distributed transactions (sagas, outbox, event sourcing where appropriate), retries, and failure recovery.
Lead architecture reviews and keep a living record of decisions (ADRs) across hundreds of services.
Identify and pay down architectural debt; plan the evolution of legacy services without disrupting live traffic.

Java and data platforms

Set Java engineering standards: frameworks, libraries, build tooling, coding practices, and JVM tuning.
Own the database strategy across relational, NoSQL, caching, and streaming platforms, including schema design, partitioning, replication, and capacity.
Diagnose and resolve performance bottlenecks across the JVM, the network, and the data layer.

Cloud, reliability, and operations

Guide the cloud architecture: containers, Kubernetes, managed data services, networking, and infrastructure as code.
Set SLOs, observability standards (metrics, tracing, logging), and incident response practices.
Drive scalability, resilience, disaster recovery, and cloud cost efficiency.
Ensure security, data protection, and auditability meet gaming regulatory and payment requirements.

Leadership

Build, lead, and mentor the engineering and technology teams; raise the bar on hiring.
Translate business goals into a technology roadmap and project plans.
Manage technical vendors and third-party platforms.
Evaluate new technology and tools and bring in what moves the platform forward.
Communicate technology strategy and risk clearly to the CEO, executives, and partners.

Required Qualifications

12+ years in software engineering, including 5+ years as an architect of large distributed systems.
Expert-level Java (Java 17+), with deep knowledge of Spring Boot / Spring Cloud, concurrency, and JVM performance tuning and garbage collection.
Proven track record designing and operating a microservices estate of 100+ services in production.
Hands-on experience with systems handling millions of real-time transactions per day, with measurable latency and uptime targets.
Deep database expertise: relational (PostgreSQL, MySQL, or Oracle) including query tuning, indexing, sharding, and replication, plus NoSQL and caching (e.g., Cassandra, MongoDB, DynamoDB, Redis).
Event-driven architecture with Kafka or a comparable streaming platform.
Production experience on AWS or GCP, with Docker, Kubernetes, and infrastructure as code (Terraform or similar).
Strong grasp of distributed-systems fundamentals: consistency models, idempotency, partitioning, backpressure, and failure modes.
Experience with API design (REST, gRPC), API gateways, and service mesh concepts.
Observability and reliability practice: Prometheus/Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Datadog or similar; SLOs and incident management.
Experience leading and growing engineering teams, and evaluating and interviewing technical candidates.
Clear communicator with executives, peers, and individual contributors.

Preferred Qualifications

Background in gaming, iGaming, sweepstakes/social casino, sports betting, fintech, or payments.
Experience with wallet, ledger, or payment systems where every transaction must reconcile.
Familiarity with gaming regulatory, PCI DSS, or SOC 2 compliance requirements.
Led a migration or re-platforming of a monolith or legacy services to microservices with no downtime.
Experience with reactive or non-blocking Java (WebFlux, Vert.x, Netty) for high-throughput services.
Cloud cost optimization (FinOps) at scale.
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent experience.
